scenes.visual: Title: “One Nerve, Many Sensory Lines”. Show separate sensory strands linking gut, airway and artery to the brainstem.

scenes.tts: The vagus carries many specialised sensory lines. Some report lung inflation and airway irritants. Others report arterial stretch, gut stretch or food. These signals help control breathing, blood pressure and feeding. So the question is what each population reports, which channel senses force, and where the signal lands in the brain. We follow the mouse evidence, from organs to sensory neurons to the brainstem.

scenes.visual: Fan the vagus into distinct sensory strands from lung, artery and gut. Pair each organ with its reported input and physiological job. Highlight the sensory route toward the brainstem; do not depict the vagus as one uniform stretch signal.

scenes.tts: Start in the gut. In awake mice, activating intestinal stretch afferents labelled O X T R strongly suppressed feeding. Activating gastric afferents labelled G L P one R suppressed it more weakly. G P R sixty five afferents responded to intestinal food, but activating them did not measurably change feeding in the assays tested. Chemical signals also reach vagal terminals through hormones released by cells in the gut lining, including cholecystokinin.

scenes.visual: Show intestinal Oxtr stretch endings and gastric Glp1r endings with qualitative feeding outcomes: strong suppression and weaker suppression. Show GPR65 villous endings responding to intestinal food, with a separate activation-to-feeding panel labelled “no measurable change in tested assays”. Add a parallel chemical route from enteroendocrine cells through cholecystokinin to vagal terminals. Keep nutrient response distinct from feeding outcome; use no numerical bars.

scenes.tts: Airway populations have different jobs too. In anaesthetized mice, light on P two R Y one afferents suppressed breathing. Light on N P Y two R afferents produced rapid shallow breathing. Driving P two R Y one afferents also recruited airway defence: closed vocal folds, swallowing and expiratory reflexes. Light shows what driving these cells can do. It does not identify their natural stimulus.

scenes.visual: Use the opposite breathing experiment once: two labelled afferent sets, light bars and schematic breathing traces under an “anaesthetized mice” label. Then show vocal-fold closure, swallowing and expiration as outputs of P2ry1 activation. Label the experiment “activation: sufficiency”; do not assign a natural stimulus to either light-driven set.

scenes.tts: Lung inflation can also halt inspiration. Deleting Piezo two in adult mouse sensory neurons impaired this inflation reflex. Arterial pressure sensing needed a combined test. Deleting both Piezo one and Piezo two from nodose and petrosal neurons abolished the baroreflex, in which rising pressure slows the heart. Neither single deletion changed it detectably. This shows a collective channel requirement, not both channels in every neuron.

scenes.visual: Show lung inflation interrupting inspiration and adult sensory-neuron Piezo2 deletion weakening that reflex. Switch to a pressure-rise/heart-slowing baroreflex diagram labelled “anaesthetized mice”. Compare single Piezo1 deletion, single Piezo2 deletion and double deletion in nodose/petrosal neurons using qualitative outcomes. The double deletion abolishes the reflex. Depict the channel requirement across the targeted population without assigning both channels to every cell.

scenes.tts: Where do these signals land? Vagal sensory axons primarily reach the nucleus of the solitary tract, or N T S, in the medulla. The brainstem processes the input. Jugular afferents take a different route, to the paratrigeminal nucleus. Some gut afferents also reach the area postrema.

scenes.visual: Follow the organ sensory strands into the medulla. Highlight the NTS as the primary target and show input being processed there. Draw a distinct jugular route to the paratrigeminal nucleus and an additional gut projection to the area postrema. Avoid a universal NTS route or a fixed one-to-one organ map.
